new_theme: MODIFY L1 (test): group-delay compensation. A 1.5 kHz float cosine (amplitude 0.8, 48 kHz) feeds a 41-tap linear-phase FIR (taps in the variable lpf_taps) -> out.dat and directly -> ref.dat; the user asks to delay the ref.dat stream by exactly the filter's group delay so the files line up sample for sample, leaving out.dat unchanged. Reference: Delay of (41-1)/2 = 20 samples on the ref.dat branch. v2 signatures: start filter|tone (test), reference delay|filter|tone (test); cluster_id chain:delay|filter|tone.

accepted.change: Resolved by the re-theme: the item no longer turns a square wave into a sine (old cell hashed to train under v2); the new function (delay alignment) is unique in the set, cluster chain:delay|filter|tone.

Moot (no stopband requirement in the new item); the enforce-what-is-stated lesson is applied as in compliance/F4.

rejected.reason: Kept L1: under the proposed level rule R7 (pending team) a single filtering stage does not by itself make an item L2, and in the new item the filter is part of the start graph; the edit is a Delay insertion. 5 functional blocks (source, FIR, delay, 2 sinks), one sample rate, no modulation.

notes: Oracle is tolerance-based on purpose (corr_ref signed, max_lag 0, >= 0.9999; zeros <= 1e-6; levels within 1 %): an FFT-filter delay (~1e-7 rounding) is valid and passes, and FIR outputs are not bit-identical across VOLK machines. Variants: Delay with (len(lpf_taps) - 1) // 2; a second FIR with pure-delay taps [0.0]*20 + [1.0]; an FFT Filter with the same taps (both filter|tone, gbf-test-10's cell, test split, listed in task notes for the reserved set). 10 mutants incl. delay before the split (p2p out.dat), ref.dat fed a filtered copy (zeros check: transient 0.35), changed taps, changed source, source level +5 % (the correlations are scale-free, the level checks catch it).
